summary: Eva Wilden is an Indologist who completed her MA (ca. 1986–1992), doctorate (ca. 1992–1996), and habilitation (ca. 1997–2004) at the University of Hamburg. She held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2003) and the University of Hamburg (2017).

Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst College under Robert A. F. Thurman and earned his PhD at the University of Toronto, also studying under Francisco Varela. His main posts include Toronto, York University, and the University of British Columbia.

Eviatar Shulman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (ca. 1999–2008), where he later served from 2009, including as department chairman around 2012 and as professor (attested 2026).

Eyal Aviv is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisors Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht and Leiden universities under C. C. Uhlenbeck, N. van Wijk, and W. Caland. He was professor of Sanskrit at Leiden University from 1939 to 1972.
Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Calgary (attested 2001), where he studied under Leslie S. Kawamura, Anthony W. Barber, and Xiaojie Yang.

Fa Yao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a pupil under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 1995). He held an attested post as Visiting Lecturer of Theravada Buddhism at the University of Chicago in 2026.

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history who earned her PhD at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences under Pierre-Étienne Will. Around 2001, she became a maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Fabio Rambelli works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Ca' Foscari University, Naples, and Tokyo, under Massimo Raveri and Adriana Boscaro. He held posts at Sapporo University (2001–2002) and UC Santa Barbara (from ca. 2010).

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" between 1969 and 2004. She has held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the University of Florence.
Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He held a post as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-Kuei Li was a linguist, Sinologist, and Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Edward Sapir. He held long-term posts at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington (1949–1969), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1969–1974).
Faren is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed a PhD at Lancaster University by 2008. In 2013, Faren was attested as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong.

Farzand Ali Durrani was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the University of the Punjab, University of Peshawar, and University of London. He served as a professor at the University of Peshawar from circa 1957 to 1993.

Fawad Khan is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. He earned a master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University, and served as Assistant Curator at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Directorate of Archaeology and Museums (attested 2022).

Fazun was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Taixu, Amdo Geshe, and Phabongkha Dechen Nyingpo, among others. He directed the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies from 1933 and served as leader of the Buddhist Academy of China (1956).
Federico Squarcini is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held posts at Ca' Foscari University of Venice around 2011 and has served as a series editor and journal editorial board member.

Feng Youlan was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at Peking University and Columbia University. He held major posts at Tsinghua University (ca. 1928–1952), the University of Pennsylvania (1946–1947), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (ca. 1947–1948).

Ferdinand Christian Baur was a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at the University of Tübingen and the Tübinger Stift (ca. 1809–1814). He subsequently held a post at the University of Tübingen from circa 1826 to 1860.

Ferdinand Hitzig was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics who studied under Heinrich Ewald (ca. 1828–1829). He held posts at the University of Zurich (ca. 1833–1861) and Heidelberg University (ca. 1861–1875).
